question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress
answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [30]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

The Registrar says a student may NOT withdraw after the published deadline [15]. If you mean seeking an exception, extraordinary circumstances beyond your control may qualify for a late administrative withdrawal. Submit an appeal letter in your own words, supported by official documentation, to the Office of the Provost no later than the last day of classes of the regular (fall or spring) semester following the term. Explain the circumstances, why standard procedures or incompletes were unavailable, and the term you wish to withdraw from. Typically, a successful appeal results in W grades for all courses in that term [16].
Withdrawing may affect financial aid and satisfactory progress toward graduation [11]. The Office of Financial Aid says students who withdraw from all classes before 60% of a semester concludes are subject to federal rules determining how much Title IV aid they may retain and must return; it highly recommends discussing any class withdrawal with Financial Aid [1]. Federal aid requires enrollment in 6 credits in a semester; falling below full-time status may reduce or remove aid [3]. SAP is reviewed annually after spring. To meet its quantitative standard, students must complete at least 67% of attempted credits toward graduation requirements; not meeting SAP can make you ineligible for aid [2].
Contact the Office of the Provost about an extraordinary-circumstances appeal, the Registrar about withdrawal procedures, and Financial Aid about your aid and SAP implications.

question: what is the policy on withdrawing from a class after the deadline and does it affect my aid/satisfactory academic progress
answer:
The Fall 2026 academic calendar lists [30]:
- Friday, October 2, 2026: Session I Courses - Last Day to Withdraw ("W" Grade) (already passed)
- Friday, November 6, 2026: Full Semester Courses – Last Day to Withdraw from Courses (“W” Grade) (already passed)
- Tuesday, November 24, 2026: Session II Courses - Last Day to Withdraw from Courses ("W" Grade)

**Registrar:** A student may not withdraw after the published deadline. Before that deadline, a withdrawal after the 50% refund period may be made through Web Self Service, using an online withdrawal form, or by completing a course withdrawal form in the Registrar’s Office [11, 15].

For extraordinary circumstances beyond your control that prevented a timely withdrawal, you may apply for a late administrative withdrawal through the **Office of the Provost**. Submit an appeal letter in your own words, with official documentation, no later than the last day of classes of the regular (fall or spring) semester following the term you want withdrawn. Explain the extraordinary circumstances, why you could not use standard withdrawal procedures or obtain incompletes, and the term. Examples include personal illness, a family member’s death or terminal illness, recovery from catastrophe or natural disaster, or immediate employer-required relocation. If appropriate, consider asking instructors for incompletes or applying for a Medical Leave of Absence [12, 16].

**Financial Aid:** Withdrawing from a course may affect financial-aid eligibility [11]. The Financial Aid page advises meeting with its office to discuss whether and how a withdrawal may affect your aid. Its federal Title IV rule described there applies to students who withdraw from all classes or leave school before 60% of a semester has concluded [1].

**Satisfactory academic progress (SAP):** A course withdrawal may affect progress toward graduation [11]. For financial-aid SAP, students must complete at least 67% of attempted credits; review is annual after spring semester. The page also gives minimum cumulative GPAs of 2.0 for undergraduates and 3.0 for graduate students [2]. The pages don’t establish the specific effect on your aid or SAP; contact Financial Aid to discuss your situation [1].

question: I got a credit balance on my student account after my aid posted, how do I get that money sent to me? Do I need to sign up for direct deposit or does it just get mailed?
answer:
Student Accounts says a Title IV financial aid credit balance of $1.00 or greater will be refunded; non-Title IV financial aid credit balances are subject to a $5.00 threshold. 4. In Payment Profile, edit or create a payment method, then check the Refund Option box to designate it for direct deposit.

Student Accounts’ direct-deposit page says refunds are deposited within one to two weeks of submitting the application, for students eligible for a refund. [2] For help, contact Student Accounts.

question: im a transfer student and i commute, how do i get a parking permit and where do i park
answer:
Orientation Programs says all students parking on campus need a current, valid permit. Apply online at the [RCNJ Parking Permits website](https://www.ramapo.edu/publicsafety/parking-permits/). Log on, enter Permit Type and click Continue; complete Contact Information, click Save/Update Person, then Continue; enter Vehicle Information and Continue; review the request and Continue. Print or save the Registration Filed page with your request number as application verification; it is not your permit. Select “student” and your correct commuter status. Commuters can register two vehicles on one hang tag at no additional fee, but each vehicle must be registered and only one may be parked on campus at a time. Permit fees are charged to your student account. New students pick up permits during New Student Check-In; returning commuters pick them up at the Public Safety ID Office during normal weekday hours, or at the Public Safety Office Main Desk after 3 pm if they email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu to request another pickup time. For parking permit questions, email parkingpermits@ramapo.edu or call (201) 684-7432. [1][7]

Public Safety says commuters may park in lots B1, B2, and B3. If your assigned lot is full, students may use C1, C2, or D lots as overflow. Commuters may not leave a vehicle parked overnight (2am – 6am) without prior authorization from Public Safety. [7][12]
